> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `26d288179ee318c482e68c152fd3eb6b26008d24` — the merge of head `a217f4bc6ca7f32a49d55069e0488a112c6ee906` into base `6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 26d288179ee318c482e68c152fd3eb6b26008d24 && git checkout 26d288179ee318c482e68c152fd3eb6b26008d24
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228 a217f4bc6ca7f32a49d55069e0488a112c6ee906 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228 && git merge --no-ff a217f4bc6ca7f32a49d55069e0488a112c6ee906

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:cli` seat 1 · `os-sales` · session `session_01BVm1pAXVXQ3PjC42j1kPFf` · 2026-10-18T00:29Z

Head `a217f4bc6`. This is the seat's review of record for #24150 (claim `6242571960`; dev report `6243580332`). No contract face is touched:
- `Clause-②: no`, with no widening or narrowing: no accept set, key, route or export moves;
- no `packages/spec/**` or `packages/metadata-protocol/**` path;
- 0 of 5 paths governed.

So CI plus the seat's own read decide it.

- **Form:**
  - Draft → `main`, titled `fix(cloud-connection): …`.
  - The body's first line is `Fixes #24150`, its only closing keyword (scanned). `Clause-②: no` is line-initial in both the body and the changeset, and matches the claim.
  - One `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/cloud-connection`.
- **The seat's own read of the code (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts` at this head):**
  - One closure, `reportedRuntimeVersion()` (`:300`), feeds both sites: `bind/start`'s two approval links (`:612`) and the bind body `bind/poll` sends (`:704`, `:712`). The plugin's `readonly version` field stays and is no longer read for the server's release.
  - A set `OS_RUNTIME_VERSION` is returned before any service read, with the old `??` set-ness. Unset, the closure reads `ctx.getService('protocol').getDiscovery()` when the handler runs, and keeps only a non-empty string `version`. Any throw, including a missing service, answers `undefined`, so the closure cannot fail a route.
  - Both reads sit after #24148's ordering (the held-session `403`, the anonymous `401`, `holdsSetupAccess`, then `CLOUD_UNCONFIGURED`), and `bind/start`'s read runs only after the control plane has answered. Nobody new learns anything.
  - Nothing is imported from `metadata-protocol`'s source and `resolveDiscoveryVersion` is not copied. The pin's `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` import is test-only and goes through the package entry, a dependency the package already had.
- **The read-failure answer (assumption 4):** A, send nothing. The seat agrees, on the four axes in the PR body. A wrong release is what the approval page would show as fact; an absent one is not a plausible string an AI or an approver can mistake. Both sites already dropped an empty value. This omits an optional emitted field on a server with no discovery producer. It changes what no caller is admitted or served, so it is not a narrowing.
- **Proof:** the pin drives the mounted routes in single and multi mode, with the expected value read from the real `getDiscovery()` on the same harness, never a literal (12 cases). The ablation restored the old fallback: 8 red and 4 controls green, then a proven restore and 12 green. On a real `app-showcase` boot, both links and the stand-in's one `/bind` request carried `18.0.0-next.3`, which is what `/api/v1/discovery` and `/.well-known/objectstack` both reported. The 93-command gate union exited 0, with eslint added for the lane blind spot.
- **Prose faces, sentence by sentence against the diff:**
  - The changeset's **Unset now**, **Set** and **No discovery document** bullets match the closure's three arms. ✓ "Nothing to rewrite" holds, since no key or route moved. ✓
  - `content/docs/deployment/cloud-connection.mdx` `#rename`: "the `version` its discovery document reports" and "`OS_RUNTIME_VERSION` is an override … sends that value as it is" match the closure. The paragraph no longer calls the fallback a known defect. ✓ No other paragraph has a hunk, as declared on #6023 (`6242576961`).
- **File surface:** `connection-credential-store.test.ts`, in the declared directory, gained a `protocol` service in its shared harness. It is test-only, forced by two version-present asserts that only the old constant satisfied, and declared in the PR's Acceptance notes. The seat accepts it inside the surface.
- **Acceptance notes:** the three in the PR body (an empty-string `OS_RUNTIME_VERSION` sends nothing while discovery reports the package version; a multi-tenant host is unmeasured; the environment-variables page has no `OS_RUNTIME_VERSION` row) are each below the filing gate and carry `carrier: none`.
- **Docs drift check** (`6243572172`): of the seven pages it lists, `cloud-connection.mdx` is the one that states this behaviour, and it changes here. The other six match on the `/api/v1/discovery` literal in the new comments, or on `getDiscovery`, and what discovery serves does not change. The release-owned `implementation-status.mdx` is untouched.
- **CI on this head:** 41 check runs, 36 success and 5 skipped (the opt-in and full-battery lanes: Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), none red, read in this act.
- **Landing:** not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 24231`: 0 of 5 paths; 286 changed lines ≤ 3000). With this record on the head, the PR goes ready with auto-merge armed in this act's next stroke.
